title.narrative: Anticipatory response to the drought in the Foz do Tapauá communities

description.narrative:
Deep within the Amazon rain forest, the State of Amazonas in Brazil had a severe drought in 2023 that was deemed to be the worst in 121 years. In direct effect, this unprecedented drought impacted 150,000 households and almost 600,000 individuals. A report issued by the Amazonas Civil Defense stated that the situation was so bad that all 62 towns in the state declared a state of emergency or alert. Local people and the scientific community indicate that the consequences of this drought persisted until early 2024, even after the rains returned. Six months after the drought began, river levels began to show signs of reduction, raising concerns among municipalities. Over 28 declared a state of emergency, and had their status recognized by the federal government, with forecasts suggesting the drought could be even more severe than last year. The Brazilian Geological Survey has presented a concerning outlook for the Amazon River Basin, with projections suggesting a 65% probability that the Solimões River will reach its lowest level ever observed. Even in regions with lower probabilities of reaching historic minimums, significant drought is still impacting the entire population, confirming that drought conditions are a reality. The state of emergency can be extended or ended depending on river levels returning to normal.
This is Caritas Brasileira Start funded project in the Amazon Region to prepare communities along the Purus River (Tapaua region) for the impending drought which will reduce water level, preventing safe travel, limiting access to food and fresh water, and cutting off families from livelihoods and markets. The total budget is £223,378.52 and the planned sectors are: Cash, WASH, Food, and Protection. The full project must be completed and 100% of funds spent within 60 days.
